definition: A Crungus is an imaginary creature found in artificial intelligence text-to-image models, sometimes also referred to as a digital cryptid.
details: Twitch streamer, voice actor, and comedian Guy Kelly found that typing the made-up word into the Craiyon image generator consistently produced pictures of a monstrous, hairy humanoid. He later tweeted about this which resulted in a very long thread of reactions and experiments with "Crungus" and variations of this AI-prompt also on different engines. Since Craiyon version 2 was introduced in 2023, the prompt "Crungus" no longer produces the same imaginary creature.

explainer.lead: Crungus is a made-up word that once reliably prompted the Craiyon image generator to draw a monstrous, hairy humanoid. Its strange repeatability made it a small internet phenomenon and a memorable example of how image generators can respond unexpectedly to meaningless prompts.

tiers.eli5: Imagine telling a drawing robot a nonsense word and getting the same kind of monster again and again. That is what happened when “Crungus” was typed into Craiyon: it produced a hairy, human-like creature. People shared the pictures and tried the word elsewhere, but newer Craiyon versions no longer make the same monster.
tiers.practitioner: “Crungus” was used as a prompt in Craiyon, where it repeatedly generated a monstrous, hairy humanoid before version 2. It can be tested as a prompt across text-to-image engines, but outputs should not be assumed to match between engines or versions. Since Craiyon version 2 was introduced in 2023, the original result no longer appears.
tiers.paperLevel: Crungus is an imaginary, humanoid creature associated with the repeated output of the nonsense prompt “Crungus” in a text-to-image model, and is sometimes described as a digital cryptid. The observation was publicized by Guy Kelly after experiments in Craiyon and subsequent community tests with prompt variations and other engines. Its behavior is version-dependent: the characteristic output ceased with Craiyon version 2, introduced in 2023.

explainer.example: Guy Kelly typed “Crungus” into Craiyon and consistently received images of a monstrous, hairy humanoid. His tweet about the discovery led other people to generate their own Crungus images and test variations of the prompt on different engines.

explainer.intuition: A meaningless word can still act as a distinctive instruction to an image generator. In Craiyon, “Crungus” happened to summon a recognizable kind of monster often enough that people treated the creature as a character of its own.
howItWorks: A user enters the invented word “Crungus” as an image prompt.
In the original Craiyon behavior, the generator repeatedly returns pictures of a monstrous, hairy humanoid.
Guy Kelly shares the result on Twitter, prompting a long thread of reactions and experiments.
Other users try the word and related prompts on Craiyon and different engines.
After Craiyon version 2 arrives in 2023, the prompt no longer produces the same creature.
explainer.whyItMatters: Crungus shows how a prompt with no ordinary meaning can produce a surprisingly repeatable visual result. Its disappearance in Craiyon version 2 also makes it a clear reminder that prompt behavior can change when a generator is updated.
misconceptions: Crungus is not a real creature; it is an imaginary figure generated from a made-up word.
The prompt does not guarantee the same monster in every engine or in current Craiyon versions.
The repeated images do not establish a general technical explanation for why the association occurred.
